original_test_intent: Verify the platform recovers from the defined DC-2 transition that removes and restores both main and standby power, then boots with complete PCIe enumeration and no unacceptable new AER or platform faults after each cycle.
original_method: After workload drain, use the vendor-approved dual-rail sequence and independent rail/console observation to prove main and standby domains reach the required states, restore them in order, and collect complete per-cycle topology and health evidence before service recovery.
manual_activity: An operator independently verifies main and standby domain transitions through the approved DC-2 sequence, maintains an alternate recovery path and authorizes workload restore only after each cycle's boot/topology evidence.
required_inputs: Exact main and standby rails/domains, controllers, BMC dependency and observable states
Vendor/platform DC-2 command/action sequence including main-off, standby-off, dwell and ordered restore
Decision whether BMC can remain available while its own standby domain is removed
Cycle count, rail timing, POST/OS timeout and total window
Workload drain, storage flush, data-loss and management-outage approval
Expected PCIe identity/link manifest and AER/DPC/BMC/storage acceptance
Independent power/rail instrumentation, console or external controller
Failed-rail, BMC-loss, boot and incomplete-restore recovery
safety_requirements: Do not assume chassis power off removes standby or satisfies DC-2
Do not remove the BMC's own recovery power without an independently proven control/restore path
Confirm exact target chassis and both domains before any action
Never expose secrets or disable host verification
Stop on ambiguous/incomplete rail transition, lost restore control, failed boot, missing/downtrained device, AER/DPC, storage/data, thermal/power fault or access loss; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact shared-code variant, domain topology and approved DC-2 state machine
Orchestrate only the documented dual-rail sequence when approved and externally observable
Collect per-state/per-cycle evidence and verify final normal domains
Perform no guessed standby action, recovery reset, retry, workload restore or verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve exact dual-rail sequence and independent recovery when BMC standby is absent
Approve cycle/timing/outage/data state and rail observers
Review every cycle and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Materially insufficient: the reused chassis off/on command demonstrates only generic host power control and provides no standby-rail action or evidence, so it cannot establish SY.5 DC-2 coverage.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-approved main-plus-standby state machine with an external controller/observer and secure interfaces; collect full per-cycle rail, boot, PCIe and error evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Main plus standby DC-2 intent, per-cycle OS/PCIe/AER checks and 10/20-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: CRITICAL DUAL-RAIL DC-2 REVIEW PENDING AUTHORITATIVE POWER-DOMAIN PROCEDURE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model main and standby domains as explicit states, prove each transition with external telemetry, restore control in the approved order, then compare normalized PCIe/link and platform health after every cycle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing standby operation, independent restore path, domain evidence and recovery while retaining the original shared-command conflict.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic chassis off/on or SY.4 result cannot prove standby-domain removal, BMC cold initialization or dual-rail restoration. Uptime/dmesg tail cannot prove those states or complete PCIe recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Removing standby can power down the management controller that issued the command, severing the only recovery channel. DC-2 therefore requires an external sequencer, facility control or documented self-restoring action whose behavior is verified independently.

project_override_considerations: If the platform cannot safely remove standby through BMC, engineering must provide an authorized external/facility procedure or mark this exact variant BLOCKED/N/A by revision; do not collapse it into SY.4.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and all shared-code variant identities
Approved main/standby domain map and authoritative DC-2 state machine
Cycle/timing/outage/data/recovery approval and secure control audit
Per-state external rail/power/BMC/console evidence for each cycle
Per-cycle boot plus full PCIe identity/link, AER/DPC/kernel/BMC/storage/thermal evidence
No-SY4-substitution/no-insecure-secret/no-auto-retry audit, both domains restored and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The exact Master procedure requires cycling both main and standby power, but the DeepSeek command is the same generic chassis off/on used for SY.4 and has no standby-domain control or proof. The supplied execution does not cover the named operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The DC-2 purpose is clear and can be statically reviewed. Execution waits for an authoritative dual-rail procedure and independent recovery rather than guessing.

engineering_decision_pending: Resolve Functionality row 1925 variant 8613c1834873ecff of shared code Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00465-V003: define the authoritative DC-2 sequence for both main and standby domains, external observation/control and recovery when BMC standby is removed; confirm cycle/timing and full PCIe/AER criteria while preserving distinction from SY.4 and SD.1.
review_improvement: Prevents the shared SY.4 command from erasing standby-power coverage and adds explicit dual-domain states, external recovery and per-cycle platform verification.
independent_technical_reasoning: Standby removal changes the initialization path of the BMC, management fabric and devices powered from auxiliary rails; a normal chassis-off command often leaves those domains alive. If the BMC loses its own power, it also cannot be assumed to restore the platform. Thus DC-2 validity depends on external state proof and a self-contained restoration mechanism, not merely successful OS boot after generic off/on.
